Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 10 g per dose, children aged 11 to 14 years take 7 g per dose, children aged 8 to 10 years take 5 g per dose, and children aged 5 to 7 years take 3 g per dose, 3 times a day after a meal.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, or by infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has an allergic constitution, has experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, itching, etc.), is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • If the symptoms do not get better after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take other antitussives and expectorants, cold medicines, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines), sedatives or the like.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one should not take this medicine.
  • Do not drink alcohol when taking it.

For an acute disease, adults take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose 3 times a day, children aged 6 to 14 years take 1 sachet (200 mg) per dose twice a day, and children aged 2 to 5 years take 1/2 sachet (100 mg) per dose 3 times a day, in each case with a small amount of water. This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, chills

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201405340. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (90 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (about 60 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (about 45 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 sachet (about 30 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 sachet (about 22.5 mL) per dose 3 times a day, in each case 30 minutes after a meal. If necessary it may be taken at bedtime, and as a rule the interval between doses is 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine or its components, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, or by infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, has a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy, is a patient who has had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine, has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia appears, if urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest appear right after taking it together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or if mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever together with rash, redness and blisters like a burn), asthma, hepatic impairment, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure, headache or myopathy (languor, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
  • People who stopped MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) within the past 2 weeks must not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with medicines for diabetes, medicines for gout, medicines for arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, throat pain and a feeling of heavi

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201701325. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 1 film per dose, 3 times a day, letting it dissolve in the mouth. The interval between doses must be 4 hours or more. Take this medicine (film) in the following order. Open the aluminum sheet, peel it away slowly from the mouth and take out only the medicine (film). (Do not swallow the whole aluminum sheet. It may lead to an unexpected accident such as the sheet lodging in the mucous membrane of the esophagus.) Place this medicine (film) on the tongue and take it while it dissolves in the saliva. This medicine (film) is a film that dissolves easily in water, so do not handle it with wet hands. This medicine (film) dissolves in the mouth immediately, but if it sticks to the throat, drink water and swallow it. Also, if there is little saliva and it is difficult to take, put water in the mouth and take it while it dissolves.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by children under 15 years of age, or by people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian medicines, etc.) or stopped taking them less than 2 weeks ago.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, is elderly, has a high fever, difficulty urinating, dry mouth, glaucoma, diabetes, thyroid dysfunction, a heart disease or high blood pressure, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 days of taking it, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, headache, convulsion, difficulty urinating, facial flushing, photophobia, symptoms of aplastic anemia (blue bruises, nosebleed, gum bleeding, fever, pale skin and mucous membranes, fatigue, palpitations, difficulty breathing, dizziness, hematuria) or agranulocytosis (high fever, chills, sore throat, etc.) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, antiparkinson drugs, etc.), other oral medicines for rhinitis, oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold remedies, antitussives and expectorants, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines, etc.), or gastrointestinal analgesic and antispasmodic medicines.

At a glance

How it works

This medicine is used for candidal vaginitis, trichomonal vaginitis, vaginitis caused by non-specific and mixed infectio

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200704064. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to insert it

Insert 1 tablet (200 mg) deep into the vagina once a day. It is advisable to insert it in the evening before bedtime. The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by newborns and infants under 6 months of age, or by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Be careful, because this medicine may weaken latex or rubber products such as condoms and vaginal contraceptive diaphragms.

Possible side effects

  • If anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) or iododerma rarely appears, if pain, itching, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use hydrogen peroxide together with this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, take 200 to 600 mg per dose 3 to 4 times a day. For mild to moderate pain and for a cold, take 200 to 400 mg per dose 3 to 4 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.   • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • When non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics including this medicine are taken, serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke that may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation, may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients who have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, by patients with severe blood abnormality, severe liver impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, by patients who have or have had bronchial asthma, by patients who have or have had a hypersensitivity reaction such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors), by patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), by pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, by patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

  • Do not take more than the recommended amount.
  • If an excessive amount has been taken, get prompt medical treatment even if there is no obvious symptom or sign.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock, anaphylactoid reaction, chest discomfort (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure; decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcer, constipation, black stools; mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reaction (unknown frequency), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash; hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction such as increases in GOT, GPT and alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver impairment; hypersensitivity, anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing, wheezing; visual disturbance such as scotoma (a blind area of the visual field), hearing loss, tinnitus, abnormal taste, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness, etc.); fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urine), hematuria, proteinuria, increases in BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalized edema, shortness of breath, languor, periorbital edema, facial edema, malaise, fever, nosebleed, edema, peripheral edema, metabolic acidosis, loss of consciousness and convulsion.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (NSAIDs).
  • People who are taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).
  • Do not breast-feed while taking this medicine.

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day.   • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

This medicine may be diluted to a lower concentration with sodium chloride solution for injection, sodium chloride solution for inhalation, sterile distilled water for injection or sterile distilled water for inhalation. For nebulization therapy using a face mask, a mouthpiece or a tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a nebulization tent or an inhaler (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases, and it is used individually according to the personal needs of the patient and the convenience of the method of administration. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes as much as about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be an amount that can maintain a very dense mist-like state inside the tent or the inhaler during the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous administration over a long period is preferable. For direct instillation, give 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the regular treatment of a patient who has had a tracheostomy, give 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When a small plastic catheter is inserted into the trachea under local anesthesia through a direct incision to give it directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree, give 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. When it is given using a percutaneous intrabronchial catheter, give 1 to 2 mL of this medicine every 1 to 4 hours with a syringe connected to the catheter. How it works

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201802564. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is elderly, has edema, has thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), has local exfoliation, dermatitis, psoriasis of the scalp or a severe burn, or has a history of heart disease.
  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

Apply it to the affected area and rub it in gently 1 to 4 times a day. If necessary, the area may be covered with gauze. In the case of contagious impetigo, it is advisable to remove the crust (scab) while taking care not to contaminate other normal skin, and then apply it.

How it works

This medicine is used for dryness and fatigue of the eyes with discomfort, a stinging pain or irritation caused by wind,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400680. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, put 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. When you put it into the eye, gently pull the lower eyelid down and put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac while looking upward.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.

  • When using a single-use product for the first time, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them, in order to remove any fragments of the container that may be produced when it is opened.
  • After opening, use a single-use product only once and discard the remaining solution and the container, and use a preservative-free multi-use product for up to 4 weeks only.
  • Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or the eyelashes.

  • Also, do not use the medicine if it has become cloudy.

  • This medicine can be used even while contact lenses are being worn.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • When you use this medicine at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

This medicine is used for the local treatment of candidal vaginitis, trichomonal vaginitis, vaginitis caused by non-specific and mixed infection and preparation before obstetric and gynecological surgery, and for germicidal vaginal washing, local washing and deodorizing.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Vaginal medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the local treatment of candidal vaginitis, trichomonal vaginitis, vaginitis caused by non-spec

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199700636. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to insert it

Dilute 30 mL of povidone-iodine 10% (available iodine 1%) in about 1 L of warm water and wash the inside and the outside of the vagina 1 to 2 times a day. For germicidal vaginal washing, local washing and deodorizing, wash 1 to 2 times a week.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), by patients with renal failure, by newborns and infants under 6 months of age, by patients with dermatitis herpetiformis, or by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients who have had a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and pregnant or breast-feeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If it has been used right before delivery, wash the newborn's eyes and bathe the baby as soon as possible after the delivery so that the medicine does not remain on the skin.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • If the undiluted solution gets into the eyes, rinse them out immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • When this medicine is used on a patient with extensive burns, provide sufficient fluids.
  • Because this medicine has a spermicidal action, do not use it if pregnancy is desired.

Possible side effects

  • Anaphylactoid symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, etc.) and hypersensitivity in the form of iododerma may rarely appear, pain, itching, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness and dermatitis may occasionally appear, and a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis and skin discoloration may rarely appear.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound treatments.
  • This medicine may damage latex or rubber products such as condoms and vaginal contraceptive diaphragms.
